label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Strained
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend substantial time on social media (averaging nearly 4 hours daily, with many exceeding 5 hours) and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their mean scores on the UCLA-8 loneliness scale, PHQ-9 depression scale, and GAD-7 anxiety scale are all notably above moderate thresholds, with anxiety symptoms being the most pronounced. This cluster of 140 respondents suggests a co-occurrence pattern linking heavy digital engagement with psychological distress.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily social-media use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily social-media usage averaging approximately 3.9 hours, with a substantial portion exceeding 5 hours
Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.78) indicating persistent feelings of social disconnection
Moderate-to-high depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 1.81)
Highest anxiety symptom levels among measured dimensions (GAD-7 mean ≈ 2.27)
Pattern of co-occurring emotional distress across loneliness, depression, and anxiety domains
tone: Concerned and empathetic; clinically attentive to the interplay between digital habits and mental health burden

label: Well-Adjusted Light-Use Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents male respondents with graduate-level education who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. Their daily social media use is relatively light, averaging roughly 2.8 hours per day (within the 1–3 hour bracket). Across all psychological well-being indicators, this group scores well below scale midpoints, suggesting generally positive mental health and moderate digital engagement.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate degree or above, 1–3 hours of daily social media use
behavior_markers: Low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.78, well below scale midpoint)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.27, near floor)
Very low anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.03, near floor)
Light daily social media consumption averaging approximately 2.8 hours
Consistent pattern of psychological well-being across all measured dimensions

label: Lonely but Low-Distress Heavy Social-Media User
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend roughly 5 hours per day on social media and report elevated loneliness, yet display comparatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite frequent social-media engagement, their psychological distress remains below average on clinical screening measures, while their subjective sense of social disconnection is notably higher.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, approximately 3–5 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Heavy daily social-media consumption averaging nearly 5 hours
Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) suggesting persistent feelings of social disconnection
Below-average depressive symptom levels (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.90)
Below-average anxiety symptom levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.85)
Possible pattern of using social media as a substitute for in-person social connection without it translating into clinical mood or anxiety disturbance
tone: Socially disconnected yet emotionally stable; quietly isolated rather than overtly distressed

label: Well-Adjusted Light-Use Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents a group of highly educated males who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms, alongside relatively light daily social-media use averaging roughly 1.6 hours. With mean scores well below clinical concern thresholds on the UCLA-8 loneliness scale (1.22), PHQ-9 depression measure (0.82), and GAD-7 anxiety measure (0.90), these respondents exhibit consistently strong psychological well-being. Their moderate-to-light social-media engagement (1–3 hours daily) aligns with their overall pattern of lower distress.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, reporting 1–3 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Light daily social-media use averaging approximately 1.6 hours
Consistently low self-reported loneliness (UCLA-8 mean 1.22 on item scale)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean 0.82)
Minimal anxiety symptomatology (GAD-7 mean 0.90)
Social-media engagement kept within a bounded 1–3 hour daily window
tone: Stable, composed, and psychologically resilient with a low-distress baseline
